data_requests.item: Existing component/service, leak-measurement and repair/verification program basis
where: site records: Existing exact component/system compressed-air service, authorized purge/drain/end-use demands, measurement method/control mode/pressure/capacity or volume/time basis, survey/repair/verification history and continuing program coverage; source/revision/units/availability and scope retained.

a walkdown: Only if existing records leave an applicable question unresolved, agree safe additional observations with the responsible engineer; no compulsory new measurement, production stop, setpoint change or retrofit.
data_requests.how: Names/counts are potential inspection clues, not actual leaks or a rate. Known hydraulic/steam components are not compressed-air leak subjects; unknown service remains conditional. Review existing suitable records first. S11 printed28-30 permits load/unload or start/stop timing estimates only with the appropriate control and actual no-demand conditions; production stopped alone does not establish that. VSD/modulating/unknown control, intentional purges/drains, active end uses and unverified boundaries require a suitable different basis, not blind use of the same timing quotient. Distinguish capacity/flow percentage from power savings and retain uncertainty. S9/S11 describe ongoing identification, repair and verification, not a program started or stopped solely by a universal5%-10% cutoff. No compulsory survey, shutdown or control adjustment is authorized.

questions.decision_rule: Review actual compressed-air service, qualified leak evidence and authorized demands, repair/verification and ongoing program coverage with the responsible specialist. Do not diagnose leakage from component labels, apply an incompatible no-load timing method or mandate a program only above a generic target. Suitable existing prevention or nonapplicability may be acknowledged; unresolved measurement/source/control/scope remains explicit. No production stop, repair instruction, compressor adjustment or site benefit follows from this screen.

typical_benefit.wording: Leaks are "often wasting as much as 20%-30% of the compressor's output"; target "5%-10% of total system flow."
typical_benefit.arc: 2.4236 (IAC/ITAC browse page: 11,223 recommendations, 0.5 yr average payback, 81.4% implemented; average dollar figure omitted)

S24: DOE IAC/ITAC database: browse pages, download, schema document

questions.limits: IAC/ITAC figures are browse-page averages read through a summarizing fetch and not re-verified against the downloadable database; averages are skewed by outliers. Source review: complete S9 compressed-air Tip3 pp1-2, with S11 printed28-30 leak methods/program and printed35-36 controls. Typical source leak percentages and example energy costs are not this system's leakage, targets or savings; scope/quantity and legitimate demand must be established.
